//: Reference .shipd-config.json covering every recognized top-level key. Copy it to .shipd-config.json (in a repo root, or a workspace root to govern every repo beneath it) and edit. All keys are optional; layers resolve nearest-wins-wholesale — the nearest file declaring a key supplies its whole value — and unknown keys are ignored, so the `// <key>` entries below are inert documentation you can keep or delete. Declared values shown are the built-in defaults, so copying this file unchanged changes no behavior.
// dir: Names the content directory holding the spec library (verified/, planned/, completed/, research/). Default `.shipd`; the config filename itself is never renamed.
// completed_retention_days: How many days a completed change stays visible to consumers. Default 30; `0` or `null` disables retention so nothing is hidden.
// store_root: Relocates the content directory into an external store, one folder per repo. No default (the content directory sits in the repo). `~` expands, and a relative value resolves against the directory of the config file that declared it.
// wiki_base: A durable base wiki store searched alongside the workspace's own wiki/. No default. Must expand (via `~`) to an absolute path.
// memory_dir: Root of the personal memory store, whose pages live in <memory_dir>/wiki. Default `~/.shipd-memory`.
// valid_themes: The vocabulary the linter accepts in an artifact's `Theme:` header. A list of strings; undeclared or empty means any theme passes. Documented in the content directory's README.md ('Theme vocabulary' section).
// autonomous-pipeline: Optional top-level key declaring the delivery pipeline: a preset name ("default", "eco", "basic") or an ordered list of stage entries. Omitted here so copying this file declares no pipeline; the full grammar lives in the content directory's README.md ('The autonomous pipeline' section).
// pr-mode: Optional top-level key choosing how a change's PR ships: "auto" (the default when omitted — an auto-merging PR) or "draft" (a draft PR, no auto-merge, a human merges). Omitted here so copying this file declares no mode; usually declared once at a workspace root, and documented in the content directory's README.md ('PR mode' section).
// guardrails: Optional top-level key holding the guardrail hook's kill-switches: `false` turns the hook off, or an object with `disable` (rule names to drop). The rules themselves are markdown files, not config — `<content-dir>/rules/*.md` in the repo, `~/.shipd/rules/*.md` for every repo, and the plugin's own `hooks/rules/*.md` built-ins, first source winning a name. Omitted here so copying this file declares nothing and the three built-in comment rules stay active; the rule file format and both modes (`deny`, `remind`) are documented in the content directory's README.md ('Guardrails' section).
// voice: Gates the plugin's session-start voice digest, the hook injecting the shipd documentation standard's conversational rules into every session. A boolean; default `true` (the digest is injected). Declare `false` to silence the hook.
// workspace: Marks the declaring directory as a workspace root and holds its registry of `projects` and the current `focus`. An empty object `{}` is a valid marker. No default (a repo is not a workspace); documented in the content directory's README.md ('Workspace' section).
// workspaces_root: The mandated parent directory under which job workspaces are created and cloned, enforced by `workspace-init` (a bare name resolves into it; a target outside it is refused) and by `/s:workspace clone`. `~` expands and the expanded value must be absolute. No default (no mandated root, and every surface behaves as it does without the key).
// post-worktree-scripts: An ordered list of shell command lines run in a freshly created worktree, e.g. copying a .env or seeding a database. Undeclared means no hooks run; register entries through `shipd worktree hooks add` (or /s:worktree-hooks) rather than by hand.
// clone_sources: Local directories the workspace sync planner probes for an existing clone of an absent member before cloning it fresh. A list of directory paths with `~` expansion; undeclared means no probing.
// lint: Configures `semdiff lint`. `run_scripts` (boolean, default false) permits the subcommand to execute a repository-defined lint script (e.g. a `package.json` `lint` script) instead of only reporting it as detected. `disable` (a list of linter names, default `[]`) names detected linters the subcommand SHALL NOT run even where a marker and binary are both present. Omitted here so copying this file runs no repository script and disables no detected linter.
// worktree_sweep: Gates whether the engine's worktree create path runs `worktree.sh sweep` after creating a worktree, reclaiming merged, guard-clean worktrees and pruning their branches. A boolean; default `true`.
// worktree_idle_minutes: The idle window, in minutes, the `remove` verb's recent-activity guard uses before a dirty worktree stops counting as freshly touched. A non-negative integer; default 30, and `0` disables the guard. `SHIPD_WORKTREE_IDLE_MINUTES` overrides it.
// worktree_stale_days: The window, in days, beyond which `worktree.sh sweep` reports an unmerged worktree's branch tip as stale on a `stale:` line rather than staying quiet about it. A positive integer; default 7. `SHIPD_WORKTREE_STALE_DAYS` overrides it.

build.//: Settings for a /s:build run and the flows sharing its config: telemetry, plus the design and video-ingest roots.
build.// design_dir: Root of the design scratch directories a plan may reference. Default `~/.shipd/designs`.
build.// video_dir: Root holding the ingested video bundles (transcript, frames, index). Default `~/.shipd/video`.
build.// video_asr: The speech-recognition backend used to transcribe a recording. Default `parakeet`.
build.// video_vocabulary: Extra domain terms biasing the transcription. A list of strings; default `[]`.
build.// video_max_frames: Cap on the frames indexed from one recording. Default 24.
build.// video_scene_floor: The fraction of that frame cap reserved for scene-change candidates, so deixis anchors cannot starve them. Default 0.25.
build.// video_cursor: Whether cursor position is tracked and drawn when grounding a frame. Default true.
